changelog: Insert a Core Principle that prescribes good cut placement for numeric expressions: keep numeral + multipliers + unit together, or if unavoidable cut before the whole phrase or after its unit — addresses the primary finding by describing a GOOD cut instead of a blanket ban.
findings: The prompt underestimates the harm of cutting inside numeric expressions (numbers, ranges, units, percentages); splitting a numeral from its unit or the endpoints of a range produces incoherent or mistranslated numeric phrases when pieces are translated separately.

The prompt undervalues keeping verbs with their core complements: it often allows cuts that strand verbs, prepositional objects, or infinitival complements, which produces orphaned predicates or reversed attachments in the joined translation.

The prompt does not sufficiently penalize cuts that create very short trailing fragments (one- or two-word pieces); such tiny fragments are frequent sources of contradiction or loss when translated separately in short-latency bins.

edits.was: - Is the preceding stretch a self-contained propositional claim, or does clause
edits.now: - When a numeric expression spans a cut, prefer cuts that keep the numeral with

diagnosis.why: Adding the numeric-preservation principle made the model prefer cuts that keep a numeral with its multipliers/units, which raised H_set on short pieces (≤10-word bins) but caused more harmful cuts in long contexts (≤99) by displacing cuts into enumerations and noun phrases; the bin breakdown (positive up to ≤10, negative at ≤99) and the tail examples show the tradeoff.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should preserve numeral+unit spans only when it does not conflict with protections against splitting heads, named entities, or enumeration boundaries in longer contexts.
